data.long_meaning: Basavaraj is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'basave' (lord) and 'raj' (reign). It is a reverential title for deities such as Lord Basaveshwara, and is also used as a personal name for boys in Hindu culture. The name Basavraj carries the meaning “Lord of Basaveshwara” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Basavraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of basaveshwara and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Basavaraj carries a rich cultural legacy in the Hindu tradition. It is a title of reverence and honour, traditionally used as a name for deities associated with power, strength, and prosperity. For instance, Lord Basaveshwara, a revered figure in the Lingayat and Baale Katchisa (veerashaiva) traditions, is an icon of courage, wisdom, and justice. This name underscores the heroic and spiritual element that forms a significant part of traditional Indian tales and folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Basavaraj holds deep spiritual significance, symbolizing the divine and authoritative presence of the supreme deity. In Hinduism, the word 'basave' represents the powerful, nurturing, and omnipotent aspects of God. The suffix 'raj' signifies the ruler or the sovereign, suggestive of God's ultimate authority and control over all aspects of creation. As a personal name, Basavaraj can be viewed as a sacred reminder of the divine influence guiding one's life. Additionally, the name is believed to bestow upon its bearer the qualities of courage, wisdom, and prosperity, making it an inspiring and empowering choice for parents in the Hindu community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Basavraj is a name revered in Hindu traditions, derived from the words 'Basava' (wild boar) and 'Raj' (rule). It symbolizes the power and fearlessness of the divine in its raw, untamed form – a reminder that even the wildest aspects of life can be ruled and tamed by the inner spirit.

historical_references.reference: Basavanna (1134-1167 CE) was a 12th-century poet-saint and social reformer from Karnataka, India. He is considered a pioneer of the Lingayat religious movement.

trends: Basavanna is a popular name among Lingayats in Karnataka
